pageDescription: AI-generated and AI-assisted research notes in quantum information science
introduction: AI4Science collects exploratory research notes developed through sustained interaction with generative AI. Each entry presents the scientific question and the scope of the result. These notes are working documents and are not intended for submission elsewhere in their current form. Future developments, if they lead to scientifically significant results, may be developed into research papers for clearer presentation and wider dissemination.

Most of the prose and derivations in these notes are generated by ChatGPT through an interactive research process. I guide the work by setting the research direction, formulating questions, checking and challenging intermediate claims, and contributing new ideas.

notes.title: Exact PVM-Incompatibility-Breaking Criterion for a Broad Class of Nonunital Qubit Channels
paragraphs: This note studies when the adjoint of a nonunital qubit channel makes every finite family of qubit projective measurements (PVMs) jointly measurable.

**Independent development and acknowledgment.** This note was generated independently by ChatGPT. Its full-rank PVM criterion, optimal parent, and uniqueness result overlap with the projective-steering results established by **Yu-Xuan Zhang, Leong-Chuan Kwek, and Jing-Ling Chen** in [EPR-steering boundaries from a universal spectral equation — arXiv:2609.14272](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14272), particularly Theorem S9 and Section S3 of the Supplemental Material.

The geometric background includes the critical-radius framework of Nguyen, Nguyen, and Gühne, [Phys. Rev. Lett. 122, 240401 (2019)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09349), which provides a characterization of projective steering and supports numerical evaluation.

Following the note's convention, **D** is the real 3 × 3 Heisenberg Bloch matrix and **t** is the translation vector. The Schrödinger action on Bloch vectors is therefore **r → Dᵀ r + t**. For invertible **D**, the **inner branch** is specified by **||D⁻ᵀt|| ≤ 1**, equivalently, the output ellipsoid contains the origin. The inverse-free condition is **DᵀD − ttᵀ ⪰ 0**, which also covers singular matrices.

Within this class, the note recovers the exact PVM-incompatibility-breaking criterion. For invertible **D**, it reduces the problem to a strictly concave optimization over three real parameters and gives a generally asymmetric optimal parent POVM with explicit classical postprocessings. The criterion extends to singular matrices by continuity. The note's construction does not determine the exact boundary outside this class.

This note builds on my research on POVM incompatibility and quantum steering. In my paper with Eric Chitambar, [Exact Steering Bound for Two-Qubit Werner States — Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 250201 (2024)](https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.250201), we showed that PVMs and arbitrary POVMs have the same steering threshold for two-qubit Werner states. My recent preprint, [Exact Incompatibility-Breaking Criterion for Unital Qubit Channels — arXiv:2607.27757](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27757), extends this equivalence to every unital qubit channel: PVMs already determine the incompatibility-breaking boundary for arbitrary POVMs.

The PVM criterion alone does not establish incompatibility breaking for arbitrary POVMs. Zhang, Kwek, and Chen also prove equality of the PVM and POVM scales for all correlation-rank-at-most-two data and for explicit full-rank bias domains (Theorems S11 and S12). Equality throughout the full-rank inner branch is not established in this note. These distinctions are essential when extending the analysis to general nonunital channels.
